memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The sun rose above him as he passed Peniel, and he was limping because of his hip. So this is why to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob's hip was touched near the tendon." - Gen 32:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the sun rises on a new day, Jacob walks on — but he walks with a limp. He came away from his encounter with God blessed and renamed, yet also wounded. He would carry that limp for the rest of his life, a permanent reminder of the night God met him and changed him.

It is worth pausing on this. Jacob did not leave his encounter with God unscathed and stronger in the old way. He left transformed but also weakened, leaning now where once he had strode confidently in his own strength. The limp was not a defeat; it was a mark of grace. Every step for the rest of his days would remind him that he had wrestled with God and prevailed only by clinging in weakness.

Sometimes God's deepest work in us leaves a mark. A hardship, a loss, a "thorn in the flesh" that never quite goes away can become the very thing that keeps us humble and dependent. The apostle Paul had such a thorn, and God told him, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness" (2 Cor 12:9).

If you carry a limp — some lasting weakness or wound from your journey with God — do not despise it. It may be the mark of a real encounter, the very place where God's strength now rests upon you. God's people often walk best when they walk with a limp.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "limp" or lasting weakness do I carry from my journey?
2. Can I see God's grace and strength even in my wounds?
3. How might my weakness keep me humble and dependent on God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your strength is made perfect in my weakness. Help me not to despise my "limp," but to see it as a mark of grace that keeps me clinging to You. Amen.
